group.name: Cisco ISE Receiver
group.description: Dashboard group for Cisco Identity Services Engine telemetry emitted by the Cisco OS receiver.

dashboards.name: 00 ISE API Trust And Deployment
dashboards.description: First-response dashboard for ISE API health, scrape completeness, service coverage, and deployment status.
dashboards.value: Proves whether ISE collection is healthy before operators trust identity, posture, policy, pxGrid, or Data Connect evidence.

charts.name: Value Provided
charts.description: Value: explains how to use the ISE API trust dashboard as the incident starting point. Interpretation: start here when ISE data is missing, stale, partially successful, or when API permissions may be hiding identity evidence.
charts.markdown:
## Value Provided
Use this dashboard first for Cisco ISE incidents. It separates telemetry trust from access symptoms: API errors, rate limits, unavailable API families, skipped services, and partial scrapes explain visibility gaps before operators trust RADIUS, TACACS, posture, policy, pxGrid, or Data Connect panels.

charts.name: Partial Scrape
charts.description: Value: proves whether one or more ISE endpoint families failed or were skipped during collection. Interpretation: 1 means the dashboard may be incomplete and should be read alongside API and service coverage charts.

charts.name: API Request Errors
charts.description: Value: surfaces failed ISE API calls by operation and HTTP status. Interpretation: non-zero values explain missing deployment, endpoint, session, policy, pxGrid, or Data Connect evidence.

charts.name: API Request Duration
charts.description: Value: detects slow ISE API operations. Interpretation: rising duration by operation can precede partial scrapes, stale dashboards, or delayed incident evidence.

charts.name: Unavailable Services
charts.description: Value: shows unavailable or skipped ISE API, pxGrid, and Data Connect groups. Interpretation: unavailable means endpoint, API enablement, role, permission, version, or credential gap.

charts.name: Deployment Node Status
charts.description: Value: tracks ISE deployment node/persona status. Interpretation: warning or failed states can explain missing authentication, posture, or MnT evidence.

dashboards.name: 01 AAA Failures Sessions And Posture
dashboards.description: Identity access dashboard for RADIUS/TACACS failures, active sessions, endpoint posture, and profile evidence.
dashboards.value: Shows whether users, endpoints, or network devices are failing authentication, authorization, accounting, posture, or profiling workflows.

charts.name: Value Provided
charts.description: Value: explains how to use ISE AAA and posture data during access incidents. Interpretation: correlate aggregate failures by bounded protocol, outcome, policy, message code, and reason; use ISE logs for user, endpoint, and network-device identities.
charts.markdown:
## Value Provided
Use this dashboard for user or endpoint access incidents. Bounded RADIUS/TACACS failure dimensions, active sessions, endpoint posture, and profiling evidence show whether the symptom is identity, policy, or endpoint compliance. Use the correlated ISE logs for user, endpoint, and network-device identity.

charts.name: RADIUS Failures
charts.description: Value: counts RADIUS authentication failures by bounded protocol, outcome, policy, message code, and failure reason. Interpretation: spikes isolate wireless, wired, VPN, MAB, or identity-store issues; use logs for user, endpoint, and network-device identity.

charts.name: TACACS Failures
charts.description: Value: counts TACACS authentication, authorization, or accounting failures. Interpretation: spikes point to admin login, command authorization, or network device administration issues.

charts.name: Active Sessions
charts.description: Value: tracks ISE active sessions and session evidence volume. Interpretation: sudden drops or spikes indicate access outages, reconnect storms, or MnT visibility gaps.

charts.name: Endpoint Posture And Profiles
charts.description: Value: surfaces endpoint posture and profile counts. Interpretation: noncompliant, unknown, or changing profile counts can explain policy decisions and quarantine behavior.

dashboards.name: 02 Policy TrustSec Alarms And Certificates
dashboards.description: Policy and platform evidence dashboard for policy objects, TrustSec, alarms, certificates, licenses, and webhooks.
dashboards.value: Correlates access failures with ISE policy state, segmentation objects, platform alarms, certificate expiry, licensing, and webhook delivery evidence.

charts.name: Value Provided
charts.description: Value: explains how policy and platform evidence narrows ISE incident cause. Interpretation: use these panels when authentication succeeds or fails because of policy, certificate, license, TrustSec, or webhook state.
charts.markdown:
## Value Provided
Use this dashboard when access behavior changed after policy, segmentation, certificate, license, or platform events. It keeps policy and operational evidence visible without turning raw rules or event text into metric dimensions.

charts.name: Policy Objects
charts.description: Value: counts ISE network-access, device-admin, TACACS, and policy objects. Interpretation: missing or changing policy object counts can explain changed access decisions.

charts.name: TrustSec Resources
charts.description: Value: counts SGT, SGACL, and SG mapping records. Interpretation: changes in TrustSec resource counts can explain segmentation impact.

charts.name: Alarms Licenses And Webhooks
charts.description: Value: surfaces ISE alarms, license state, and webhook delivery evidence. Interpretation: platform alarms, license failures, or webhook delivery failures can explain missing downstream evidence.

charts.name: Certificate Expiration
charts.description: Value: shows ISE certificate expiration timestamps. Interpretation: certificates close to expiry can disrupt EAP, portals, pxGrid, or API trust.

dashboards.name: 03 pxGrid And Data Connect Coverage
dashboards.description: Full-coverage dashboard for pxGrid service/subscription state and Data Connect query health.
dashboards.value: Confirms that opt-in pxGrid streaming and Data Connect historical reporting are working before operators depend on those high-fidelity ISE feeds.

charts.name: Value Provided
charts.description: Value: explains how to validate opt-in pxGrid and Data Connect coverage. Interpretation: use these panels when REST evidence is present but real-time session signals or historical RADIUS/TACACS rows are missing.
charts.markdown:
## Value Provided
Use this dashboard for the optional high-fidelity ISE feeds. pxGrid panels prove service lookup and subscription intent; Data Connect panels prove database view access, row caps, and query health.

charts.name: pxGrid Service And Subscription Status
charts.description: Value: shows pxGrid service lookup and configured subscription state. Interpretation: missing services or failed subscriptions explain absent real-time session, RADIUS, endpoint, TrustSec, or system health signals.

charts.name: pxGrid Messages
charts.description: Value: counts pxGrid messages or REST query objects by type. Interpretation: changing message volume proves the feed is active and can reveal session or RADIUS failure bursts.

charts.name: Data Connect Query Health
charts.description: Value: tracks Data Connect query duration and error rate by view. Interpretation: slow or failing views point to wallet, TLS, credential, database, or view availability problems.

charts.name: Data Connect Rows
charts.description: Value: shows rows returned by each allowlisted Data Connect view. Interpretation: unexpected zero rows or sudden spikes reveal coverage gaps, row-cap pressure, or incident bursts.
